evaluations.prompt: Use Kerncap to isolate the kernel that takes the most GPU time in my HIP app, mini_pipeline.hip, into a standalone reproducer under ./isolated, replay it, and check it reproduces the captured run. Write report.md with the kernel you chose and why, the reproducer path, the replay timing, and the validation result.
expected_behavior: Ranks the application's kernels with Kerncap and picks the kernel with the highest total GPU time from that ranking, saying why
Extracts that kernel with Kerncap into a reproducer under ./isolated, passing the workspace as the source directory, then replays it and runs Kerncap validation
Reports the replay timing and the validation result taken from Kerncap's output, and notes that validating without an edited kernel only confirms the capture replays
unexpected_behavior: Chooses the kernel by reading the source instead of profiling, or reports timings or a validation result that do not appear in Kerncap's output

evaluations.prompt: Use Kerncap to isolate the vector_scale kernel from my HIP app, mini_pipeline.hip, into a standalone reproducer under ./isolated and replay it for 50 iterations to get a stable time. Write report.md with the reproducer path and the replay timing.
expected_behavior: Extracts the vector_scale kernel with Kerncap into a reproducer under ./isolated, passing the workspace as the source directory
Replays the reproducer with Kerncap for 50 iterations and reports the timing from Kerncap's output in report.md
unexpected_behavior: Extracts a different kernel than vector_scale, or reports a timing that does not appear in Kerncap's output

evaluations.prompt: How do I pull the slowest GPU kernel out of a llama.cpp benchmark run into a standalone reproducer I can iterate on without rerunning llama-bench every time?
How do I capture one Triton kernel from a PyTorch training run on an MI300X so I can replay, edit, and check it on its own without rerunning the whole training loop?
Benchmark vLLM throughput and time-to-first-token for Llama 3 on this MI300X.
Capture an end-to-end rocprofv3 timeline of my training run so I can see CPU and GPU overlap.
